A deeply unsettling robot dog bearing the eerily realistic face of Elon Musk was spotted mid-walkies on the streets of San Francisco this week. The robot is part of the Regular Animals project by Beeple, aka Mike Winkelmann, created in collaboration with mask-maker Hyperflesh and built on Unitree Go2 robot dogs. Art foundation NODE told WIRED the robots were taken out on a walk to promote Beeple’s upcoming exhibition in Palo Alto. Other versions of the robot dog feature the faces of Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos, Andy Warhol, Pablo Picasso, and Beeple himself.

XPENG’s humanoid robot, known as IRON, represents the company’s expansion beyond electric vehicles into robotics and embodied AI. XPENG, a Chinese EV manufacturer founded in 2014, has leveraged its expertise in electric drivetrains, AI software, and autonomous systems to develop robotic platforms capable of dynamic movement and real-time environmental interaction. Humanoid robots like IRON rely on advanced motion planning algorithms, electric actuators, and sensor fusion systems - typically combining cameras, LiDAR, inertial measurement units (IMUs), and force sensors. These systems allow the robot to maintain balance, adjust posture, and perform coordinated movements that appear fluid and human-like. Modern humanoid locomotion depends heavily on real-time feedback control. Small positional corrections are made hundreds of times per second to stabilize joints and prevent falls. This is similar to the control architecture used in self-balancing robots and autonomous vehicles. XPENG’s broader robotics initiative aligns with a global push toward general-purpose humanoid platforms - machines designed to operate in human environments rather than factory-only settings. While still in early development stages, such robots are being researched for applications ranging from logistics and manufacturing to service roles and human-robot interaction studies. Industrial humanoid robots are looking less humanlike every day.  The Chinese company LimX Dynamics just shared footage of its TRON 2 dual-arm robot integrated with an industrial robotic arm. The TRON 2 multi-form-factor robot has gone viral in the past for its modular design that can transform into a humanoid, a quadruped, or even be combined into a centaur.    In the industrial setup, TRON 2 is mounted onto a traditional robotic arm to extend its reach. It uses a custom attachment to hold and operate a power drill and nailer to assemble wooden frames and panels. It then applies spray finishing.    The TRON 2 is priced starting around $7,000 in China but international pricing begins around $13,000.   Shenzhen-based LimX is scaling production of its TRON platform, along with its full-sized humanoid robot Oli, and its sister, Luna, after securing around $400 million so far in 2026. Valued at $2.2 billion, it's one of many Chinese robotics startups racing toward a public listing. #robotics #robot #industrialrobot #ai #automation

The "robot" appearance is just a suit, likely made for fun, social media content, or a promotional stunt.   Real context:   There ARE real cooking robots being developed in China and elsewhere — but they don’t look like this, and they move much more mechanically. This is purely entertainment / viral content, not real technology. 😄  發生了什麼事：   這個人物正在鍋裡攪拌和扔食物——但對於真正的機器人來說，這些動作太流暢、太自然了。  「機器人」的外觀只是一套套裝，可能是為了好玩、社群媒體內容或促銷噱頭而設計的。   真實背景：   中國和其他地方正在開發真正的烹飪機器人——但它們看起來不是這樣的，而且它們的移動更加機械化。這純粹是娛樂/病毒式內容，而不是真正的技術。  Chuyện gì đang xảy ra:   Hình vẽ đang khuấy và ném thức ăn vào chảo - nhưng các chuyển động quá linh hoạt và tự nhiên đối với một robot thực sự.  Ngoại hình của "robot" chỉ là một bộ đồ, có thể được tạo ra để giải trí, nội dung trên mạng xã hội hoặc đóng thế quảng cáo.   Bối cảnh thực tế:   Có những robot nấu ăn thực sự đang được phát triển ở Trung Quốc và các nơi khác - nhưng chúng trông không giống thế này và chúng di chuyển một cách máy móc hơn nhiều.
